page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v6 is a Ddsv6-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor with 64 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, the CPU includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

The server is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. For local storage, it includes a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, offering high-capacity, low-latency storage directly attached to the instance. This hardware configuration does not include any GPU accelerators. The balanced ratio of compute resources to memory positions this instance within the general-purpose category, with the integrated NVMe storage enhancing its utility for data-intensive operations.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance across several domains, though with notable tradeoffs. The instance achieves top-tier status in static web serving throughput, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. It also demonstrates strong performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, Passmark CPU tests, software compilation, and Redis SET operations. However, memory performance presents a bottleneck; while small-block cached read bandwidth is strong, the Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25%, indicating potential limitations under memory-intensive workloads that exceed cache limits.

Given these characteristics, the D64ds_v6 is suited for high-throughput static web serving, database operations, and software development pipelines such as Clang compilation. The presence of AMX and AVX-512 instructions enables strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference for small to medium models, though text generation for larger 70B models drops to average levels. The combination of 64 vCPUs and 3780 GB of local NVMe storage makes it highly capable for relational databases, caching layers, and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring local scratch space.
